title: The Ants That Turn Into Living Jars of Honey
subject: honeypot ant

scenes.text: Some ants never leave the nest. They hang there as food.
They're honeypot ants, and a few are chosen to become living jars.
Workers feed them until their bellies swell to the size of a grape. Then they can barely move.
In two Australian colonies, nearly half the ants were these living jars.
When food runs short, workers stroke their antennae, and the jar hands back its honey, mouth to mouth.
People eat them too. Aboriginal Australians dig up to two meters down to reach a nest.

description:
Some ants never leave the nest. They hang from the ceiling as jars of honey.
Honeypot ants fill special workers called repletes with nectar until their bellies swell to about the size of a grape, and the colony drinks from them when food is scarce. In two Australian colonies studied, nearly half the ants were repletes.
Would you rather be a worker or a jar?
first_comment: In Colorado's Garden of the Gods, honeypot ant nests fell by 58 percent between 1975 and 2018. What tiny animal would you want to protect?
